decisions.rationale: Gholdengo at 11% dies to anything and its remaining chip is small, but its Thunderbolt (46-80% vs Mega Zard-Y) is half our Charizard answer, so I preserve it by pivoting to Sinistcha, which shrugs off Knock Off (29-70%) and High Horsepower (12-28%) and has Strength Sap/Rage Powder to heal and redirect later. decisions.rationale: Matcha Gotcha is 4x on Swampert and its SpD is already -1: ~90-165% of max HP, so from 63% it's a near-certain KO (Sitrus can't save it), plus Sinistcha drains HP back. selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Scrafty)
decisions.rationale: Swampert's Wide Guard (+3 priority) safely blocks Sinistcha's 4x super-effective Matcha Gotcha spread attack from hitting Swampert or Scrafty. decisions.notebook: Series score 1-1 (Game 3). Opponent team: Gholdengo (Occa Berry, Good as Gold), Rotom-Heat (Sitrus Berry, Levitate), Tyranitar (Chople Berry, Sand Stream), Excadrill (Life Orb, Sand Rush), Floette-Eternal (Floettite), Sinistcha (Heatproof, Leftovers knocked off).

decisions.rationale: Rage Powder absorbs Swampert's Liquidation (12-23% on Sinistcha) and Scrafty's now item-bonus-less, burned Knock Off, so Rotom pivots out to Floette-Eternal completely free instead of eating a likely-lethal Liquidation (Floette would take ~27-79% on a raw switch). reflections.notebook:
SERIES vs this opp: Scrafty/Swampert/Goodra-H/Dragapult is the standard bring; Charizard-Y and Venusaur consistently benched (they have never been brought vs our Fairy/Steel core).
TENDENCIES: Scrafty Fake Out+Intimidate then Snarl spam (spread, ignores Rage Powder; Roseli Berry blunts one Fairy hit; kill early). Swampert: no Protect, Wide Guard (used repeatedly)/Yawn/Sitrus. Goodra-H spams Flash Cannon/Body Press, Protects when low or when read. Dragapult: Focus Sash, one Dragon Darts then endless Phantom Force cycling, never switches, keeps looping at 1 HP. Charizard megas T1 then Protects. Venusaur Life Orb Sludge Bomb.
MECHANICS (verified): Phantom Force charge turn = fully invulnerable, so ANY attack or Strength Sap aimed at it is a wasted turn (logs as a 'miss'); only the strike turn is targetable. Target re-resolves on the strike turn, so Rage Powder must be up that turn; Infiltrator does not bypass redirection, and Phantom Force breaks Protect. Slower attacker still lands its KO after the strike resolves, so pair redirector + attacker. Sap Sipper blocks Strength Sap. Good as Gold blocks Yawn/WoW/Snarl. Fairy is immune to Dragon Darts. Wide Guard blocks our spread moves.
DAMAGE lvl50: Gholdengo Shadow Ball vs Dragapult 75-141% (2HKO floor); Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha vs Dragapult 13-25%; Dragapult(-2) Dragon Darts vs Gholdengo 4-8%, Phantom Force vs Sinistcha 29-50% (unboosted 58-100%); Mega Floette Energy Ball OHKOs Swampert through Sitrus; Moonblast vs Goodra-H 30-50% (two-shot).
PLAN: Core bring = Sinistcha (redirect) + Gholdengo (status immunity, Shadow Ball wincon)

reflections.summary: Bringing Swampert and Hisuian Goodra into Mega Floette and Sinistcha created severe type vulnerabilities to Grass/Fairy coverage, allowing Sinistcha's Rage Powder to completely redirect single-target attacks while Dragapult was forced into predictable Phantom Force turns.
reflections.adjustment: At team preview, avoid bringing Grass-vulnerable anchors like Swampert into Sinistcha/Floette cores, and prioritize faster direct spread damage or Taunt/Pyschocontrol to bypass Rage Powder and punish Fragile Fairy/Ghost cores.
reflections.notebook: Opponent strategy: Relies heavily on Sinistcha (Heatproof) Rage Powder redirection to enable Mega Floette (Fairy Aura) and Gholdengo (Occa Berry). Dragapult (213 Spe) outspeeds opponent's entire roster (Mega Floette max 169 Spe, Gholdengo max 136 Spe, Sinistcha max 122 Spe).
